paragraphs.text: Hybrid mana (also known as half-half mana ) is a type of mana first seen in Ravnica: City of Guilds . Each hybrid mana symbol represents a cost which can be paid with one of two colors .

Hybrid mana is a complex design proposition for a mechanic used to give players flexibility. The idea for hybrid mana was inspired by the opposing "and" and "or" logical operators , i.e., prior multicolor cards required both colors of mana, while hybrid cards require only one. A deck of using either color could cast a spell with the hybrid cost between them.

Ostensibly, the spell should live in the overlap of the two colors, but the context of the color pie usually means one side is lopsided in its representation: a card like Scarscale Ritual is a standard Black effect, but is a strange cost for Blue to pay for a mana's discount, and Giantbaiting is common in Red but a temporary creature in Green has only occurred when combined with mechanics like Echo or Cumulative upkeep . This has led to some color breaks (such as mono-blue gaining life through Augury Adept , when blue has no access to lifegain.) and is cited as one of the reasons hybrid is considered full multicolor for color identity . It also has some level of "aesthetic bending", a phenomenon generally exclusive to hybrid cards, which lets a color that is primary in something get a weakened version it usually won't see on a monocolor card, as it reads oddly for that color. Examples are Don & Raph, Hard Science with blue menace when blue has unblockable, Pumpkin Bombardment having black creature damage when black has superior removal options, and Wild Cantor being a functional green ritual when it can get mana creatures.

A quirk of the mechanic is that it lets designers make a multicolored one-drop, which can be further beneficial for two-color aggro decks, but naturally is serviceable in aggro decks of either color. Two- or three-mana spells with two hybrid pips, however, are best played in the matching color pair as they are usually risky to play when half of one's manabase can't contribute. Hybrid can also be used to reinforce monocolored gameplay with even denser mana costs: running both Wasp Lancer and Ashenmoor Gouger in a blue-red deck is not recommended, but a mono-black deck can run both with no difficulty. Throne of Eldraine repeated this with a cycle of cards like Loch Dragon . Some hybrid designs reinforce the color pie by having two options but requiring the appropriate color to access their effect.
Hybrid mana symbols can be of any combination of two colors or any color of mana and either colorless mana or two generic mana . In textual terms, hybrid mana symbols are represented as:

Before officially being introduced, two cards were developed in this space: Vaevictis Asmadi , which had triple-hybrid firebreathing , and Jungle Troll , which had hybrid red-green to regenerate. Without the proper symbology, they used three and two abilities with the same output.

Hybrid mana was introduced in Ravnica block as part of the multicolor theme. It became one of Ravnica's many returning themes, with a common, uncommon, and rare cycle when the plane was revisited in Return to Ravnica block and Guilds of Ravnica block . The Extort mechanic in Gatecrash is the first time a hybrid mana cost ( ) was integrated into the rules of a mechanic.

Shadowmoor block used hybrid as the major mechanic in a contrast to the subtypal themes of Lorwyn block , to the point that R&D realized that they had overstretched hybrid's design space . It was also featured in Alara Reborn as an easier way to play three-colored cards, as was the theme of the block, and also in a much smaller role in Fate Reforged , where it reflected the erasure of a wedge's third color.

During the sets between the Guilds of Ravnica block and Strixhaven: School of Mages , the usage picked up considerably. It appeared in the uncommon planeswalker double-cycle in War of the Spark ; the quad-hybrid double-cycle in Throne of Eldraine as a set of monocolor payoffs; three multicolor cycles and the Companion double-cycle in Ikoria: Lair of Behemoths to smooth out a wedge theme; a single two-brid card ability in Zendikar Rising ; a cycle in Jumpstart ; and five cycles in Strixhaven: School of Mages (the most in one set since Shadowmoor ).

Only one card in the next four sets ( Tatsunari, Toad Rider in Kamigawa: Neon Dynasty ) used hybrid. Still, the three-color set Streets of New Capenna brought a cycle with a new hybrid cost structure, along with a cycle of hybrid activated ability creatures. The Phyrexian hybrid mana cost associated with compleated was the only hybrid cost for the year 2023, and Huatli, Poet of Unity used hybrid for an ability.

The return to Ravnica in Murders at Karlov Manor is not an explicitly multicolor set, but as it uses Ravnica as a setting, it has a higher density than normal. To represent the guilds without the excess of mana fixing, hybrid returns in a greater density to ease color requirements, on a cycle of split cards and a full set of common morphs, and three other high-rarity cards otherwise. It also appears on two double cycles in Ravnica: Clue Edition . Then, hybrid spells were used on the spell half of a full cycle of MDFC dual lands in Modern Horizons 3 alongside a triple activation on Shilgengar, Sire of Famine , then in a double cycle of common creatures in Bloomburrow . Tarkir: Dragonstorm saw the return of two-brid on two cycles of three-color cards.

Marvel's Spider-Man / Through the Omenpaths was a set developed around the new Pick-Two Draft format, which involves a much smaller set size with fewer commons and uncommons. The nature of picking two cards at a time meant that Design found it easier to cut off access to one or more colors during the draft and subsequently made it frustrating for players to pivot to a new color pair, as there were only the five allied ones that were supported. Increasing the number of hybrid cards in the set allowed Design to increase the number of playable options for each color pair within the set's smaller size. The set included three sets of hybrid ally color cycles: common, uncommon, and rare. Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles would use a similar approach, but with two common enemy color cycles and a double cycle of rares. Avatar: The Last Airbender also has common and uncommon double cycles, which, alongside a basic land counting cycle, encouraged some monocolor decks. Rosewater and R&D have found a small amount of hybrid to be generally beneficial to Limited play.

Lorwyn Eclipsed , as a sequel to Shadowmoor as much as Lorwyn, integrates the multicolor nature of hybrid into its design more strongly than using it as a workhorse draft experience. It includes the new Vivid mechanic and "color-spent matters".
In 2017, Hybrid mana became considered to be deciduous . In 2026, Hybrid mana crossed the barrier from being deciduous to evergreen .

Shadowmoor introduced monocolored hybrid cards (also called " two-brid "). Before that set, there was an earlier version which was effectively "three-brid" in the Shard cycle of Mirrodin . Monocolored hybrid mana symbols represent a cost that can be paid in either of two ways. For example, can be paid with either or with two mana of any type. It's a black mana symbol. Two-brid returned on an ability in Zendikar Rising ( Tazri, Beacon of Unity ). It saw full mechanical implementation in Tarkir: Dragonstorm to lighten the mana requirements of some of its wedge -colored cards.

A card with a monocolored hybrid mana symbol in its mana cost is each of the colors that appear in its mana cost, regardless of what mana was spent to play it. It is not colorless. For example, Beseech the Queen above is black, even if you spend six red mana to play it. These are also referred to as "two-brid".

A card with monocolored hybrid mana symbols in its mana cost has a mana value equal to the highest possible cost it could be played for. Its mana value never changes. For example, Beseech the Queen above has a mana value of 6, even if you spend to play it.
If a cost includes more than one monocolored hybrid mana symbol, you can choose a different way to pay for each symbol. For example, you can play Beseech the Queen by spending , , , or .
If an effect reduces the cost to play a spell by an amount of generic mana, it applies to a monocolored hybrid spell only if you've chosen a method of paying for it that includes generic mana.

Unlike other hybrid cards, which appear in two-tone frames, the Shadowmoor monocolored hybrid cards appear in monocolored frames because they're just a single color. When it appeared in Tarkir: Dragonstorm , the gold cards were framed like other conventional gold cards.

Some monocolored hybrid cards may appear as color pie breaks, such as Kin-Tree Severance , which allows green to have access to non-creature-based removal. Mark Rosewater has explained that they are not considered breaks, as they are comparable to colorless cards , which have access to every ability.

Devin Low initially proposed "two-brid" mana for Shadowmoor as a way to give hybrid mana a twist that could redefine what it meant to be a hybrid card, in the same way that hybrid mana had originally redefined what it meant to be multicolored. The symbol itself came as a flash of inspiration during a design meeting in the Ivory Tower conference room. "Two-brid" mana allowed the design team to reward players for building monocolored limited decks by making cards more powerful at a lower mana value compared to decks that were using multiple colors. Tarkir: Dragonstorm's example did the same for full clan decks.

Secrets of Strixhaven takes two-brid in a new direction by blending it with Converge . Casting for one color is the cheapest version but also the lowest Converge value, but choosing the two-generic mana cost can expand the number of colors. As both cards using this design have an additional ability granting a converge-like ability to other spells, getting it down cheaper can be desirable. Hence, it still encourages many colors but creates a different incentive when castable cheaply.

As part of the Eldrazi theme in Modern Horizons 3 , Wizards of the Coast introduced a new set of monocolored hybrid symbols where the non-color half is colorless mana. For example, can be paid with either or . It's a blue mana symbol. Ulalek, Fused Atrocity is the only instance of any of these symbols.

Phyrexian hybrid mana was introduced in Kamigawa: Neon Dynasty . Phyrexian mana can already be paid in two ways, while Phyrexian hybrid mana allows for the payment in three ways: one of two colors or for 2 life. While the rules handle all ten forms of Phyrexian hybrid mana, only four Planeswalkers with the Compleated mechanic have been printed with the symbols.

In the 2009 set Alara Reborn , hybrid symbols were featured alongside the "normal" mana symbols for the first time. For example, Jund Hackblade costs . As Alara Reborn was composed of all multicolored cards, it filled the slot of a card that could conceivably cost and be playable in any red deck but was still multicolored. As the format was built on shards , a deck and subsets thereof being unable to cast it was not a consideration. The mana cost of is representative of the allied colors of red, black, and green. Black and green are enemies, though they are both allied with the main color, red, or . All the hybrid cards in the set follow this patterning; thus, all hybrid symbols were of enemy colors.

Hybrid mana has not been a design focus for many years, and as such, costs of this nature have not been seen for a while. Ikoria: Lair of Behemoths showed the other side in the five Apex creatures, which are wedge-colored and have a Mutate cost that has an allied hybrid (i.e. ) and their common enemy ( ) in the cost ( Nethroi, Apex of Death , normal cost , mutate cost ). Strixhaven: School of Mages showed a brand-new cost in the form of XMHN, where H is a hybrid cost of M and N — such as Quandrix Cultivator ( ). This is the first time the hybrid cost was between two color symbols.

Streets of New Capenna inverted the Strixhaven style with three-colored cards that could be played in a monocolor deck of the shard's central color, i.e. center color N, flanked by M/N and N/O hybrid mana, where M and O are the allied colors to N. Ognis, the Dragon's Lash , for example, costs . This would be the first time since Reaper King that a card had multiple unique hybrid mana in its cost.
Leyline of the Guildpact has a uniquely asymmetrical cost of ; it is playable entirely in mono-green, but it is possible to cast with the other four.

The digital card Providence of Night has all five hybrid allied mana in its mana cost. The minimum colors needed to cast it would be MMNNO, where MN are enemy colors, and O is either color that completes a wedge . Logically, a card with five hybrid enemy mana would do the same for a shard.

Nephilim Epochal has a four-hybrid mana cost, mixing two enemy and ally, with one black and one blue symbol. As befitting a Nephilim Commander, it can be cast through any unique four colors, and as such it could be deduced that there are multiple configurations in which this is true. There are more limited options for casting it with fewer colors: it could be cast with only , and six of the ten three-color combinations can cast it, excluding the four that have their complementary color pair hybrid symbol in its cost (Abzan, Esper, Grixis, and Temur cannot cast it).
